A.name: Day and month swapped (DD/MM vs MM/DD)
A.description: The date that reaches the invite, reminder or calendar has day and month exchanged: booked 7 April, the invite says 4 July (and the reverse). In every parseable report both numbers are 1-12, so the date is ambiguous; no report has a day of 13 or more. That points at a parser that reads a numeric D/M date as M/D whenever that is valid, and probably falls back to the other order otherwise. Weekday names in the reports always match the real 2026 weekday of the date they go with (91 dated weekdays checked), so the weekday is computed from the wrong date; there is no separate weekday bug. It shows up in all 11 tenants, all 12 browser locales (en-US included), all 3 channels, both booking-v2 and booking-v3 forms, and both intakeTags.

examples: Our 7 April reminder went out on 4 July. Is this a joke. It is not April Fools where we are.
Thursday 8 January showed as Saturday 1 August. I moved it myself.
Invite says Friday 7 August. We agreed Wednesday 8 July. Which one do I trust?

B.name: Date shifted by one day / timezone
B.description: The date is off by exactly one day, or differs between recipients in different timezones, with no day/month swap. Typical cause: a date-only value stored as a UTC midnight timestamp and shown in another timezone, or an all-day event converted per recipient. Examples: invite says Tuesday 12 May, calendar says Monday 11 May (+1 day); Tuesday 6 October shown as Monday (-1 day); a Lisbon client got Tuesday and a Toronto client got Monday; every booking in June one day off; an invite timestamp earlier than the booking itself. This matches the desk's "oneDayMove" list exactly.

examples: Invite says Tuesday 12 May. Calendar says Monday 11 May. My client turned up on the Monday. We had coffee.
Client in Lisbon got Tuesday. Client in Toronto got Monday. Same meeting. We held it twice.
Tuesday 6 October showed as Monday. I moved it myself. I have stopped reporting these but my colleague says it helps you.

flags.R-41236: weak: no dates; "invite arrived before booking" implies a timestamp shift (timezone), not a swap; included because the desk put it in oneDayMove

C.name: Comments / feature requests, no concrete incident
C.description: Messages with no specific wrong date that comment on the day-first problem: asking for a "day first" setting and a workaround of saying dates in words. They point at the same root cause as A but do not describe a separate incident.

examples: Is there a setting for "my country writes the day first". I have looked. I would pay for it.
I have started telling clients the date in words. "The second Tuesday." It works. Your product is now a phone call.

U.name: Unclear
U.description: Says "the wrong day" with no dates, so it cannot be told apart from A or B.

examples: Your software sent my mother to the dentist on the wrong day. She went anyway. They fitted her in. This is not a complaint about the dentist.
